audit.whatIsWrong: Lane difficulty framing was gender-broken (Ahri called 'he/his/him' in 16 fields) and the level chart disagreed across layers: full phases[].side read Ahri/Skill/Skill/Skill/Ahri/Skill/Skill while content win[] and packet.levelChart both read Fizz/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz.
audit.why: Fizz is melee with a 550-range Q and no ranged answer until 6; Ahri's Orb of Deception is 970 range on a flat 7s and Charm is 975 on a flat 12s, so she owns levels 2-5. Level 6 Chum the Waters plus the Playful/Trickster untargetable window flips it, which is why the 52.95% winrate sits on Fizz's side.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides realigned to the content layer and the packet: Fizz L1, Ahri L2-L5, Fizz L6 onward. Whys rewritten in the same proposal to match each new verdict. All 16 misgender findings fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes and phases[5].why asserted the string 'one-shots squishies' — a magnitude with no source in either kit.
audit.why: Neither Riot description gives damage numbers; the real spikes are level 3 (Playful/Trickster online, 16s at rank 1), level 6 (Chum the Waters, 120s at rank 1, knockup that lands through Spirit Rush's dashes) and first item.
audit.corrected: Spikes restated as mechanical: L3 pole, L6 shark holding her through Spirit Rush, first item making the string lethal. Kept 4 spikes[] entries, no count change.

audit.whatIsWrong: Charm (E) was described as a ROOT in three places (content.early, spikes[0].text, wants.foe[1]); Fox-Fire was labelled '(Q)' in spikes[0].text when it is Ahri's W; Chum the Waters was described as a ROOT in spikes[1].text and content.mid; Seastone Trident was credited with a 'true-damage execute' that appears nowhere in Riot's text or the derived flags.
audit.why: Riot's Charm text: damages and charms, 'instantly stopping movement abilities and causing them to walk harmlessly towards her' — it is a charm that cancels dashes, not a root. Fizz's R text: slows, then 'knocking up the target' — a slow plus knockup, not a root. Fizz's W text is a bleed with an auto reset; the kit carries only the autoReset flag, no trueDamage and no execute. Ahri's Q is the ability with the trueDamage flag (true damage on the way back).
audit.corrected: Charm restated as a charm that stops movement abilities; Fox-Fire relabelled (W); R restated as slow-then-knockup; Seastone Trident restated as a bleed. Added the decisive interaction the page never stated: Charm instantly stops movement abilities, so it cancels Urchin Strike and the Playful/Trickster hop mid-motion — E must be held for her cast, never spent as an entrance. Also added the missing-interaction finding: Essence Theft heals her every ninth minion, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades.
sources: enemyKit E text (hardCC, 'instantly stopping movement abilities')

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' for a 12-second ability.
audit.why: Charm is 12s flat at every rank; Playful/Trickster is 16/14/12/10/8; Spirit Rush is 140/120/100.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns and the Do's bullet corrected to twelve seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two dosFull/dontsFull bodies were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted verbatim under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED on dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d).
audit.why: The title promises one idea and the body explains a different one.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles, grounded in Charm's cast timing and the untargetable frames.

edits.before: Ahri outranges you badly before level 6 — her Orb of Deception (Q) chunks your HP every time you step up to farm, and if she lands Charm (E) you're rooted for a full auto-attack-and-Q combo that can nearly kill you at level 3. Play from max range, only trade when her E is on cooldown, and use your E's second-cast dash purely to dodge her Charm rather than to engage. Ward tri-brush since she loves flanking with Charm from the side. If she misses Charm while clearing a wave or checking a ward, that's your window to jump in with Urchin Strike and land free damage before she can reset spacing.

Play from max range, only trade when her E is on its flat 12s, and use your E's second-cast dash purely to dodge her Charm rather than to engage. Ward tri-brush since she loves flanking with Charm from the side. If she misses Charm while clearing a wave or checking a ward, that's your window to jump in with Urchin Strike and land free damage before she can reset spacing.

edits.before: Level 6 flips this hard in your favor — Chum the Waters roots and marks for a huge burst combo that Ahri's Spirit Rush can't fully escape if you land it in melee range, and your Playful/Trickster jump lets you dodge her Charm on the engage. Look to all-in the moment she uses Q to push or clear, since without Orb of Deception up she has no way to disengage your dive. Group for mid-game roams too — your Urchin Strike-into-Seastone burst deletes squishies faster than her Charm-Q-R combo can peel, forcing her to play passively once you hit 6.
edits.after: Level 6 flips this hard in your favor — Chum the Waters slows and then knocks up, so her three Spirit Rush dashes cannot carry her out of it, and your Playful/Trickster jump dodges her Charm on the engage. All-in the moment she spends Q to clear: Orb is a flat 7s and without it she cannot chip you off the dive. Essence Theft heals her off every ninth minion, so buy Grievous Wounds before you plan on extended trades. Group for mid-game roams too — your Urchin Strike-into-Seastone burst punishes squishies faster than her Charm-W-R combo can peel, forcing her to play passively once you hit 6.

edits.before: With Nashor's Tooth or Lich Bane online your empowered auto-into-Q trades win almost any short trade, and Seastone Trident's true damage punishes her lower HP pool in all-ins. She still threatens from range with Spirit Rush poke chains in teamfights, so flank through fog or river brush with your E jump to land on her directly rather than approaching in a straight line where she can kite and Charm you first.
edits.after: With Nashor's Tooth or Lich Bane online your empowered auto-into-Q wins almost any short trade, and Seastone Trident's bleed keeps ticking while she tries to walk it off with Essence Theft. She still threatens from range with Spirit Rush chains in teamfights, so flank through fog or river brush with your E jump to land on her directly rather than approaching in a straight line where she can kite and Charm you first.

notes:
CHART: the full layer and the content layer disagreed on every row. content win[] (Fizz/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz) matches packet.levelChart exactly, so the FULL layer was the wrong one and I moved phases[N].side onto the content values. That means these seven side edits have NO paired win[N] edit — not because one was forgotten, but because win[N] is already the correct value on disk and an edit would be a no-op the applier would reject. After this proposal applies, the two layers agree. Please do not read the absent win[N] twins as the unmatched-side defect the brief warns about.

SuspectNames were both FALSE POSITIVES: 'Seastone Trident' is Fizz's real W and 'Chum the Waters' is his real R. The genuine ability error in this matchup was different — spikes[0].text called Fox-Fire '(Q)' when it is Ahri's W, and three fields called Charm a root when Riot's text says it charms and stops movement abilities.

UNSOURCED CLAIM REMOVED: Seastone Trident was credited with a 'true-damage execute' in spikes[3].text and content.late. Fizz's W carries only the autoReset flag and Riot's text describes a bleed — no true damage, no execute. Ahri's Q is the ability with trueDamage. I removed the claim rather than restate it.

TEMPLATES LEFT STANDING (judged templated, could not ground in Ahri's kit without inventing): breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, ahead, breakdown.mid, winCon. Each would paste onto any mid enemy with the name swapped, but nothing in Ahri's kit gives a specific replacement fact, and the brief's rule is that a surviving template beats a fabrication.

report[] edits are limited to the four the lint flagged for misgendering plus the two trade strings they quote — no discretionary report rewrites.
